scope.summary: Complete payment-card numbers and IBANs are strong candidates for deterministic extraction followed by format and checksum validation. This supports reducing model use for these entity types, but does not establish real-document recall or justify removing all Presidio capabilities.
included: Payment-card primary account numbers (PANs), including compact and explicitly supported separated representations.
IBAN country codes, country-specific lengths and BBAN structures, MOD-97-10 checksums, and original-text spans.
Public source inspection of Presidio 2.2.364 and python-stdnum 2.2, with upstream data freshness distinguished from release behavior.
excluded: Proof of account existence, ownership, issuance, activation, balance, payment authorization or current bank membership.
CVV/CVC, expiry dates and domestic non-IBAN account formats.
Application source inspection or modification, external validation of local identifiers, and production benchmarking.

iban.authority: SWIFT is the ISO 13616 registration authority. The retrieved official PDF is release 103, September 2026; its history identifies a Brazil update. Some indexed document-centre content still described release 102, so the downloaded document was checked directly.
iban.structure: Two country letters, two check digits and a country-specific BBAN of at most 30 alphanumeric characters: at most 34 characters overall. A registered country has a fixed length and BBAN structure; an arbitrary ISO country code is insufficient.
iban.checks: Normalize an accepted representation, enforce country and complete format, then verify MOD-97-10. Rearrange the first four characters to the end, replace A through Z by 10 through 35, and require remainder 1. These checks do not establish account existence.
iban.swiss_example: CH has length 21 and a BBAN consisting of five digits followed by twelve alphanumeric characters. SWIFT prints CH9300762011623852957 as CH93 0076 2011 6238 5295 7.

payment_cards.structure: ISO/IEC 7812-1 defines issuer identification and PAN structure. ISO's explanation of the eight-digit IIN transition gives a maximum PAN length of 19 and a minimum of 10 for issuers using eight-digit IINs. Historical six-digit-IIN formats had a broader minimum. A common-card detector's 12-19 or 13-19 policy must therefore be stated as a coverage choice, not a universal ISO rule.
payment_cards.checksum: Luhn is a useful deterministic check for the supported payment-card profile. It does not identify the issuer, prove that a number was issued, or show that a payment will succeed.
payment_cards.issuer_ranges: Avoid a permanently hard-coded rule that cards must start with 3, 4, 5 or 6. Stripe publishes a Mastercard 2-series test PAN, 2223003122003222, which must be included in coverage tests.

validation_layers: Extraction identifies a candidate span in text; it must preserve offsets and cannot prove validity.
Format validation enforces the chosen PAN profile or the registered IBAN country, exact length and character positions.
Checksum validation rejects many transcription errors but is not a semantic classifier.
Issuance and ownership are outside these offline checks. A documentation example can pass every arithmetic check without being a real customer's account.

separators_and_extraction.status: Engineering recommendations, not claims of measured extraction quality.
normalization: Extract on the original text and keep start/end offsets; normalize only the candidate sent to the validator.
Use ASCII [0-9] for numeric rules. For IBAN, allow an explicit ASCII case-insensitive input policy and uppercase the candidate for validation.

Enumerate supported separators: ordinary space, U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE, U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE, and optionally ASCII hyphen. Their acceptance is a detector policy; it does not make every such rendering an official bank presentation.
Bound the number of separators between characters or groups. Do not use unbounded \s* or remove all non-alphanumeric characters from a document: both can join separate values, lines or table cells.
Do not silently correct OCR substitutions such as O/0 or I/1. If required, evaluate a separate recovery path and distinguish the original text from a proposed correction.

pan_candidates.length_policy: A broad current PAN candidate profile can use 10-19 digits; a narrower common-payment-card profile can use 12-19 with its exclusions documented. Apply length after removing only allowed separators.
pan_candidates.important_limit: This is a candidate fragment, not a complete extractor. It still needs token/layout boundaries and a check against selecting a valid-looking substring of a longer separator-connected numeric run. A bare word boundary does not solve the separated-run case.
pan_candidates.grouping: Support documented renderings such as 4-4-4-4 and Amex 4-6-5; do not assume that all cards have four groups of four digits. Context or layout is needed where consecutive unrelated numeric fields resemble a card.

iban_candidates.preferred_flow: Find a plausible two-letter country and two-digit checksum prefix, look up the registered total length, collect a bounded candidate using the configured separator policy, then validate the complete canonical value. Standard compact and grouped forms should be covered first.
iban_candidates.limits: Never consume an unbounded alphanumeric-and-space run. The complete canonical value cannot exceed 34 characters; with at most one separator between characters, its raw span is bounded as well. Preserve country-code/check-digit adjacency for the standard profile.
iban_candidates.boundaries: Test punctuation, adjacent letters, trailing prose and following numbers explicitly. A country-aware endpoint helps avoid swallowing words after a valid IBAN, but a detector must also reject contiguous overlong tokens instead of salvaging a valid prefix.
iban_candidates.line_breaks: Keep newlines, HTML element boundaries and table-cell boundaries outside the baseline separator set. Add line-wrap recovery only with layout-aware tests, because a global whitespace matcher can merge unrelated fields.

validators_and_libraries.name: python-stdnum
validators_and_libraries.version_examined: 2.2, released 2026-01-04; public 2.2 IBAN source and documentation inspected.
validators_and_libraries.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later, as declared in the module headers.
validators_and_libraries.iban_behavior: stdnum.iban.validate checks MOD-97, requires an entry in its IBAN database and validates the complete BBAN structure. check_country=False disables optional country-specific modules; it does not disable the base country lookup or BBAN format check. Country-specific domestic checks exist only for some countries.
validators_and_libraries.normalization: IBAN compacting requests removal of spaces, hyphens and periods and uppercases the result. Constrain extraction first; a permissive normalizer should not define document boundaries.
validators_and_libraries.pan_behavior: The public format inventory exposes stdnum.luhn as a generic checksum algorithm, not a dedicated credit-card extractor or issuer/length validator. Combine Luhn with explicit PAN extraction and format policy; do not invent a stdnum.creditcard API.
validators_and_libraries.data_freshness: The inspected upstream master iban.dat identifies registry v101. SWIFT now publishes v103. [uncertain] Exact deployed 2.2 database parity with v103 was not audited here; a release number alone does not prove current country coverage.

validators_and_libraries.name: Presidio CreditCardRecognizer
validators_and_libraries.version_examined: Public tag 2.2.364; the inspected main source has the same candidate pattern.
validators_and_libraries.license: MIT; the project license requires preserving its copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions.
validators_and_libraries.behavior: Uses a candidate regex, optional context, removal of ordinary spaces/hyphens and a Luhn check. These operations are deterministic and are not an LLM-based card detector.
source_derived_limits: The default pattern's group lengths total 13-17 digits. This is narrower than the 12-19 range often described for the entity.
Its allowed prefixes omit 2, so the published Stripe Mastercard 2-series example cannot match the default regex.
The separator class accepts ASCII space or hyphen, not NBSP, narrow NBSP or newlines.
Amex 4-6-5 grouping is not automatically a failure: optional separators allow the six-digit group to split into two internal groups of three.
validators_and_libraries.interpretation: These are code-level coverage observations, not measured rates of missed real cards. The parent audit owns runtime verification against the installed package.

validators_and_libraries.name: Presidio IbanRecognizer
validators_and_libraries.version_examined: Public tag 2.2.364; the microsoft repository release URL redirects to data-privacy-stack/presidio.
validators_and_libraries.behavior: Extracts grouped candidates, removes ASCII spaces/hyphens, checks the generated IBAN check digits and consults country regexes. Its group fallback tries shorter candidate endings to avoid including trailing text.
source_derived_limits: The default exact_match=False causes country validation to use re.match without a required end anchor; it is not equivalent to full-string country-length validation.
The default extraction flags are DOTALL and MULTILINE, with uppercase character classes. Case-normalizing after a match does not guarantee lowercase input was extracted.
Default extraction separators are ASCII space and hyphen; broader validator normalization cannot recover candidates that the extractor never selected.
validators_and_libraries.country_table: The inspected upstream iban_patterns.py embeds a manually maintained table and cites Wikipedia and other secondary references. Do not treat it as a live copy of SWIFT. [uncertain] An exhaustive comparison of the tag's country patterns against registry v103 was not completed.
validators_and_libraries.interpretation: Require full candidate format validation independently of the matching score. A score raised by checksum success is not a calibrated probability that the text is PII.

supplied_source_audit.status: [uncertain] The article body could not be retrieved through the web tool despite direct, trailing-slash and category-link attempts.
supplied_source_audit.verified: The site's accessible developer-resources index lists the article, dated 2026-06-17, and describes generic and DE/GB/FR/NL regexes plus the limits of regex-only validation.
supplied_source_audit.not_verified: The actual regexes, checksum code, edge cases, claimed coverage, maintenance process and reuse license were not inspected. Do not present an audit of these details as completed.
supplied_source_audit.decision: Treat this commercial vendor article as a supplied secondary source, not the country-format authority. Its broad description is consistent with layered validation, but implementation choices should be checked against SWIFT and maintained library source.

supplied_source_audit.status: Retrieved; created 2021-04-09, with two revisions shown.
findings: The anchored expression is a whole-value shape matcher, not an extractor for arbitrary prose.
It permits any two uppercase country letters and a generic length envelope, with no lookup of the registered country's exact BBAN structure or length.
It does not calculate MOD-97. Matching its positive sample list cannot establish rejection of checksum-invalid values.
The pasted Kotlin-style expression includes quoting and escape text in its separator class; its exact portability and accepted punctuation must be tested in the intended regex engine.
The sample table is illustrative rather than a maintained authority; no evidence was found that it tracks current SWIFT releases.
supplied_source_audit.license: [uncertain] No explicit reuse license was visible on the inspected gist page. Do not assume that public visibility grants the same permissions as MIT or LGPL.
supplied_source_audit.decision: Do not adopt it as the complete validator. Use SWIFT-backed country data plus a maintained checksum implementation, with a separately tested extractor.

false_positives: Luhn is also used outside payment cards. For uniformly random numeric strings of a fixed length, exactly one possible final digit per prefix passes: the resulting one-in-ten property is mathematical, not a measured document false-positive rate.
IBAN examples, test cards, synthetic numbers and unrelated structured strings can pass checksums. Their presence does not prove personal ownership.
Overly permissive separator removal can combine independent fields into a checksum-valid number.
A validator accepting a prefix instead of the complete candidate can accept a wrong-length value.
Repeated-digit or all-zero candidates can satisfy some checksum algorithms; issuer/profile rules and clearly defined synthetic-data treatment are separate decisions.
false_negatives: Unsupported grouping, NBSP, narrow NBSP, lower-case IBANs, OCR mistakes, masks, line wrapping and markup boundaries may prevent extraction before a validator is called.
Country-table lag, outdated issuer prefixes and arbitrary PAN length restrictions exclude valid formats.

Strict checksums reject mistyped real identifiers. If the product aims to detect attempted disclosure as well as valid identifiers, preserve a separate explicitly lower-confidence path rather than silently broadening the valid category.
Mandatory nearby keywords can miss bare table cells. Removing all context can increase classification errors; measure that trade-off.
false_positive_and_recall_risks.unmeasured: [uncertain] No representative labeled corpus, recall comparison with Ministral, precision estimate, latency benchmark or production coverage percentage was available. The listed failure modes cannot be converted into real-world rates from source inspection.

detector_recommendation.decision: Use deterministic extraction and validation as the primary path for complete literal PANs and IBANs. A small custom recognizer or correction of existing recognizer configuration is preferable to replacing the entire Presidio framework for these two types.
detector_recommendation.iban: Reuse stdnum.iban for validation when available; enforce the extraction policy and full canonical format, and monitor country-data updates against SWIFT. Retain the distinction between generic IBAN validation and additional domestic checks.
detector_recommendation.cards: Use bounded candidates, an explicit supported length/issuer policy and Luhn. Cover Mastercard 2-series and 19-digit candidates. A checksum helper alone is not a card recognizer.
detector_recommendation.ministral: Complete well-formed literals do not need generative reasoning to apply their formal rules. Keep any model-based handling of masked, corrupted or contextual disclosures as a separately evaluated use case rather than assuming it is redundant.
detector_recommendation.replacement_gate: [uncertain] Removal of Ministral for these entity types should depend on paired evaluation on labeled representative documents, including exact spans and formatting variants. Removal of Presidio as a whole cannot be justified from this financial-identifier review.
evaluation: Compare current detector, deterministic candidate pipeline, and their union on the same documents.
Report entity precision and recall, exact-span correctness, and latency separately for cards and IBANs.
Stratify by country, PAN length/prefix, separator, case, prose/table/code context, and masked or erroneous input.
Keep synthetic acceptance checks separate from real-document recall measurements; choose acceptable non-regression criteria before switching.

acceptance_cases.status: Proposed tests for the host implementation, not a claim that an application test suite was run. Named public examples are test/reference data, and generated checksum-valid values imply no issuance.

positive_cases.expected: Extract a complete PAN candidate and pass Luhn.
positive_cases.origin: Stripe public Visa test number: https://docs.stripe.com/testing

positive_cases.expected: Accept supported separated forms; preserve the full original span, including separators.
Recognize the published Mastercard 2-series test PAN; detect the default Presidio prefix coverage gap.
Accept the Amex 4-6-5 rendering when that payment-card profile is supported.
positive_cases.origin: Grouped representation of the Stripe public Amex test number: https://docs.stripe.com/testing

positive_cases.expected: Extract all 19 digits and pass Luhn in a profile allowing 19 digits; no issuer or issuance claim.
positive_cases.origin: Synthetic arithmetic test, independently checked with a local standard-library Luhn calculation.

positive_cases.expected: Accept compact/printed IBAN and the explicitly supported lowercase normalization; retain original spans.
positive_cases.origin: SWIFT public CH reference example and a derived lowercase variant: https://www.swift.com/swift-resource/9606/download

negative_and_boundary_cases.expected: Reject as a checksum-valid PAN; a separate suspected-disclosure policy may retain it at a different confidence.
Reject IBAN checksum after successful candidate extraction.
Reject the full 23-character candidate despite MOD-97=1, because the registered DE length is 22. This targets unanchored country validation.
negative_and_boundary_cases.origin: Synthetic wrong-length value with recalculated checksum, calculated locally.
Synthetic unknown-country value with recalculated checksum, calculated locally.

negative_and_boundary_cases.expected: Do not extract a valid substring from the overlong contiguous run. Do not join lines or accept a masked IBAN through the baseline full-identifier path.
Preserve the exact IBAN span beside punctuation/prose; reject the contiguous overlong IBAN token; exercise the explicit degenerate-PAN policy rather than trusting Luhn alone.
